title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment-I
summary: A 40.6 cm x 94 cm cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) fabric was burned in two successive tests aboard an uncrewed Cygnus spacecraft at 20 cm/s air flow: concurrent spread over approximately 84 cm, followed by opposed spread over the approximately 10 cm of remaining fuel.

normal_gravity_reference.note: 1-g burn length reported as Complete; spread rate Acceleratory (no constant rate).

tests.notes: Thickness corrected to 0.37 mm using 20170008805.pdf, Table I (p. 29); the PSI CSV labels 0.37 as cm, which would convert to 3.7 mm. Pressure is not reported in the consulted sources; 101.3 kPa assumed as nominal ISS cabin pressure. Gravity level 1e-6 g is the repository convention for orbital microgravity. CSV sample length/width labels appear transposed relative to the Readme and results report: original sample 94 cm long by 40.6 cm wide. Ignition 182 W for 8 s. Burn duration 420 s; approximately 84 cm burned out of 94 cm, so classified partial_burn. Airflow was switched off to extinguish the flame. O2 21.6% is the midpoint of the reported 21.5-21.7% range; Table I footnote i states oxygen values were derived from measured CO2 production relative to the initial ISS O2 reading.

tests.notes: Thickness corrected to 0.37 mm using 20170008805.pdf, Table I (p. 29); the PSI CSV labels 0.37 as cm, which would convert to 3.7 mm. Pressure is not reported in the consulted sources; 101.3 kPa assumed as nominal ISS cabin pressure. Gravity level 1e-6 g is the repository convention for orbital microgravity. CSV sample length/width labels appear transposed relative to the Readme and results report: original sample 94 cm long by 40.6 cm wide. Ignition 182 W for 8 s. Burn duration 70 s. S2 is a second ignition of the approximately 10 cm remaining on the same physical fabric after S1, rather than a new 94 cm sample; complete_burn refers to this remaining fuel (Table I, sample 1-2). O2 is approximately 21.5%, not an exact measurement; Table I footnote i identifies O2 as derived from CO2 production relative to the initial ISS reading. The near-zero 1-g burn length does not distinguish no ignition from immediate extinction; review the normalized reference outcome.
